name: Rezin
title: The Last King of Aram
summary: Rezin was the last king of Aram (Syria) with its capital in Damascus. He allied himself with Pekah, king of Israel, against Judah under King Ahaz, in what is known as the Syro-Ephraimite War. He was eventually defeated and killed by the Assyrian king Tiglath-Pileser III.

keyEvents.title: Alliance with Pekah against Judah
keyEvents.description: Rezin, the king of Aram, allied himself with Pekah, the king of Israel, to attack Jerusalem and depose King Ahaz of Judah, replacing him with a puppet king.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's Prophecy to Ahaz
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah assured King Ahaz that the alliance between Rezin and Pekah would not succeed, and prophesied the sign of Immanuel as proof of God's protection.

keyEvents.title: Threat against Judah and the House of David
keyEvents.description: Rezin and Pekah attempted to capture Jerusalem and install 'the son of Tabeel' as king, which threatened the Davidic line of succession.

keyEvents.title: Rezin Recaptures Elat for Aram
keyEvents.description: Rezin succeeded in driving the Judeans out of the port city of Elat on the Red Sea and gave it to the Edomites, a significant military loss for Judah.

keyEvents.title: Ahaz Seeks Help from Assyria
keyEvents.description: King Ahaz of Judah sent tribute to the Assyrian king Tiglath-Pileser III and asked him to rescue him from Rezin and Pekah, initiating Judah's vassalage to Assyria.

keyEvents.title: The Fall of Damascus and the Death of Rezin
keyEvents.description: Tiglath-Pileser III attacked Damascus, captured the city, deported its inhabitants to Kir, and killed Rezin, marking the end of the Aramean kingdom in Damascus.
